claims.text: The governing distance measure is the GPS polyline, not the rounded trip-record copy. EV-GPS-00520 records trace_distance_km 5.63 against a booked optimal of 3.1 km on EV-TRIP-00520; the excess is 2.53 km, or 81.6% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment limbs pass (81.6% > 20% and 2.53 km > 0.8 km) and the excess also crosses the 50% material-deviation gate, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The trace that carries the finding is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 121 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0. There is no gap over 90 seconds (limb a), no 500 m jump between consecutive fixes (limb b) and no sustained interval above 30 seconds (limb c), so the impairment consequences in POL-RD-07 do not fire, the finding may rest on the gps_trace alone under POL-RD-08(b), and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Nothing moves the baseline off the booked optimal route: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route; trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play; and pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal. POL-RD-02 therefore runs against the booked 3.1 km / 6.0 minute optimal, not against some larger figure the driver might prefer.

On POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary: charged_total 12.53 on EV-FARE-00520 less recomputed_fare 8.605 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.1 + 0.28 x 6.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee — leaves 3.9250, which the platform's own derived figures publish as a payable refund of SGD 3.95 once rounded up to the nearest 0.05. It clears the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and is 31.3% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's remedy on this record is a partial refund of about SGD 3.95 and not nothing.

The rider's chat message on EV-CHAT-00520 does record a request to stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501, so POL-RD-04 can excuse part of the excess — but only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and the record nowhere quantifies that figure: the derived GPS block reports a single material deviation and no waypoint-attribution distance at all. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact for the exoneration he invokes, and an unquantified attribution cannot FULLY excuse a 2.53 km excess. To the extent it excuses part, POL-RD-02 still runs, and runs against the adjusted optimal route.

POL-RD-04 excludes excess DISTANCE and nothing else: unlike POL-RD-03, which spells out how an adjusted optimal's duration is derived (scaled by the ratio of adjusted to booked distance), POL-RD-04 carries no duration limb, so the booked 6.0-minute optimal duration governs the POL-RD-02 recomputation. The rider was billed 20.0 charged minutes at 0.28/min — a time_fare of 5.60 — against that 6.0-minute optimal. Whatever the detour attribution does to the distance line, the excess time charge the rider actually paid is not reached by POL-RD-04 and remains refundable under POL-RD-02.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip. EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING), so it can carry no fact and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run by anyone: no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the trace, or supports a leave-and-rejoin. No external traffic or closure exoneration is therefore available to cut down the measured excess.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and this case is triable on a monetary ruling rather than held. The trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00520, EV-GPS-00520 and EV-FARE-00520; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no timestamps run backwards (the trace runs 11:36:40 to 11:56:40); the POL-RD-02 refund of 3.9250 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total 12.53; and every charge line — base fare 3.80, distance 2.33, time 5.60, platform fee 0.80, zero ERP — has its counterpart in the trip record.

POL-RD-08's extra corroboration condition does not bite on this rider: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, below the 4-claim trigger, and the excess at 81.6% is itself above the 30% threshold the condition names. The deviation claim therefore needs no corroboration beyond the gps_trace.

The driver's SGD 1.90 is the POL-RD-04 compensation limb — 2.53 unbilled kilometres at 0.75, rounded up — and it is both discretionary ('may be granted') and conditional on the same rider-attribution the exoneration limb requires, measured against the trace rather than the trip record's rounded copy. It is not a refund of the fare and it must never be set against any POL-RD-02 refund the rider is owed: POL-GEN-03 requires a rider refund and a driver payment to be recorded independently, and forbids netting them.

claims.text: The rider herself asked for the extra stop, in the in-app chat: at 11:37:10 she wrote 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something'. That is a rider-side instruction, so POL-RD-04(a) is satisfied on the face of the export.

The instruction is timely under POL-RD-04(b): the trip record shows the journey started at 11:36:40 and the rider's request was sent at 11:37:10 and delivered at 11:37:11 — inside the first minute of the trip and far within the three-minute window the clause allows after the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor.

The message is not the vague 'go the fast way' the clause excludes. It names a specific place and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint — 'Sheng Siong Supermarket, Blk 501 Tampines Central 1', lat 1.3549, lng 103.9458 — so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test is runnable on the record rather than undecidable as it would be on a null hint. The rider's own counter-statement confirms the point: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.'

The gps_trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 121 fixes over 20 minutes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 s (well under 90 s) and a sustained sampling interval of 10 s (well under 30 s). There is accordingly no POL-RD-10(3) escalation on this trace and the case is decidable on the present record.

The trace corroborates a genuinely longer drive on this trip: the driven polyline measures 5.63 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 3.1 km, a measured excess of 2.53 km or 81.6% over optimal. That is the signature of a stop at the rider's off-corridor Sheng Siong waypoint, and the rider admits she asked for it.

The driver was billed for less distance than the trace records, and the shortfall is large: fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 3.1 km, equal to the booked optimal, while gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 5.63 km — 2.53 unbilled kilometres, comfortably past the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. The rider paid for the route she booked, not the route she asked the driver to drive.

The compensation follows arithmetically under POL-RD-04: 2.53 unbilled kilometres at SGD 0.75 per kilometre is SGD 1.8975, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 1.90 — the exact sum the driver contests. The SGD 15.00 per-trip cap is nowhere near reached.

Even if the deviation were treated as standing rather than exonerated, it is MATERIAL (81.6% exceeds the 50% material threshold), so POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile check — and that check comes back clean. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, below both the three-flag test and the 0.05 ratio test. No pattern is established, so the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) and the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) are both unavailable; the profile fields used are the two POL-RD-06 names and no other, per POL-GEN-01.

To the extent the excess is attributable to the rider's own recorded instruction, POL-RD-04 requires it to be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, so no distance-or-time refund runs back to the rider and the charge already levied against her stands. The money that moves on this case therefore moves to the driver: under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd carrying the same SGD 1.90 figure as driver_compensation_sgd.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The deviation itself is real and is measured on this trip's own instruments: the GPS trace on EV-GPS-00520 runs 5.63 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against the booked optimal of 3.1 km on EV-TRIP-00520, an excess of 2.53 km, or 81.6%, which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment limbs (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and crosses the 50% materiality gate. But the driver is not at fault for it. The in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00520) records the rider asking at 11:37:10, one minute after the 11:36:40 start and well inside POL-RD-04's three-minute window, 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', carrying a platform-resolved waypoint_hint (Sheng Siong Supermarket, Blk 501 Tampines Central 1), and the rider confirms it in her own statement: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.' POL-RD-04 therefore exonerates the excess. The rider's argument for a SGD 3.95 partial refund under POL-RD-02 is rejected: POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it, and POL-RD-04 fully excuses this one, the whole 2.53 km being the requested supermarket stop with no other cause of excess in evidence. The rider's further point, that POL-RD-04 excludes excess distance but not excess time, does not survive either: POL-RD-02 is triggered by a POL-RD-01 distance deviation, and once that deviation is exonerated the recomputation does not run, so the time line as billed stands. What the record does show is that the driver was paid for only the booked 3.1 km while the trace records 5.63 km - a shortfall of 2.53 unbilled kilometres, past POL-RD-04's 1.0 km gate. That clause pays SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.53 x 0.75 = SGD 1.8975, rounded UP to the nearest 0.05 = SGD 1.90, far under the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and the amount the ruling moves is SGD 1.90, which is also the figure in driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's own charge is not refunded, and under POL-GEN-03 the driver payment is not netted against any rider refund. On the remaining points: the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00520-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) can carry no fact, so no POL-RD-03 traffic exoneration exists and none is needed, because the driver relies on the rider's instruction and not on an external traffic cause - the absence neither cuts the excess nor engages POL-RD-10(5). No POL-RD-10 escalation fires: trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00520, EV-GPS-00520 and EV-FARE-00520; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) with 121 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and no gaps; no timestamps disagree; the amount is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total 12.53; and every charge line (base fare 3.80, distance 2.33, time 5.60, platform fee 0.80, zero ERP) has its counterpart in the trip record, so no billing-integrity referral arises under POL-RD-09(4). The driver_profile check comes back clean - deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, below both POL-RD-06 tests - so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

To both parties — here is what the evidence decides.

1. The detour is established, but it was the rider's own request. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00520, weight 1.0) records 5.63 km driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-00520) is 3.1 km. The excess is 2.53 km, or 81.6% over optimal — over both POL-RD-01 thresholds (20% and 0.8 km) and over the 50% material gate. But POL-RD-04 exonerates an excess caused by a rider instruction recorded in the chat log. At 11:37:10, about one minute into the trip, the rider wrote in the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00520): 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', carrying the platform-resolved waypoint (1.3549, 103.9458) for Sheng Siong Blk 501 Tampines Central 1; the driver replied 'ok'. The rider's own statement confirms this: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.' The instruction came from the rider, was sent well inside the three-minute window POL-RD-04(b) allows, and names a place specific enough to act on, with a non-null waypoint_hint — so the clause's corroboration test is runnable and is satisfied. The whole 2.53 km excess is attributable to that requested stop; nothing else on the record accounts for the extra distance. The excess is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run, no deviation remains, and no distance-or-time refund arises. In any event the rider was billed only 3.1 km on the distance line (EV-FARE-00520), so she never paid for the detour distance.

2. The driver is owed the unbilled distance. The fare billed 3.1 km while the trace records 5.63 km — an unbilled shortfall of 2.53 km, over POL-RD-04's 1.0 km gate. At the policy rate of SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, 2.53 x 0.75 = 1.8975, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 1.90 — the exact sum the driver contested, and far under the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. Under POL-GEN-03 this is a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling: amount_sgd carries the same SGD 1.90 as driver_compensation_sgd. It is a payment to the driver, it is NOT netted against the rider's fare, and the rider's charge stands as billed (NO_ACTION on the charge).

3. Checks run. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (121 fixes, 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, empty gaps array, max inter-fix gap 0 s, no jump over 500 m, no interval over 30 s), so POL-RD-10(3) does not apply and the finding may rest on the trace. No traffic advisory is on file: EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no closure exoneration is available — the driver invokes none and does not need one. Because the deviation is material, POL-RD-06 required the driver-profile check: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, below both pattern tests, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00520, EV-GPS-00520 and EV-FARE-00520, the timestamps agree and do not run backwards, the refund ceiling is not approached, and every charge line (base 3.80, distance 2.33, time 5.60, platform fee 0.80, zero ERP) has its counterpart. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty.

4. Claims answered. The rider's argument that the detour cannot be quantified, and her separate argument that POL-RD-04 has no duration limb so the time charge survives, are rejected: the record quantifies the total excess (2.53 km); the rider's request with its resolved waypoint, her admission that she asked for the stop, and the trace's otherwise-unexplained excess together attribute the whole of it; and with the excess fully excluded no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider's points that the trace is unimpaired and that the missing advisory removes any POL-RD-03 exoneration are accepted, but they do not change the outcome. The driver's POL-RD-06 point (no pattern) is accepted; his POL-RD-04 exoneration and compensation claims are accepted and are the basis of this ruling.

To both parties: this dispute is about a stop the rider asked for, and the driver's claim for the distance he actually drove.

What happened. The booked trip was metered, about 3.1 km from Our Tampines Hub to Pasir Ris, with a booked optimal time of 6.0 minutes. At 11:37:10, about 30 seconds into the trip (started 11:36:40), the rider messaged in-app: 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', and the driver replied 'ok'. The rider confirms this in her own statement: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.'

Route deviation (POL-RD-01). The governing distance is the GPS trace, 5.63 km on EV-GPS-00520, not the rounded trip-record copy of 5.6 km. Against the booked optimal of 3.1 km that is an excess of 2.53 km, or 81.6%, which passes both establishment tests (81.6% > 20%; 2.53 km > 0.8 km) and the 50% materiality gate.

Rider-requested stop (POL-RD-04). The instruction came from the rider, was sent inside the first minute of the trip (well within the 3-minute window), and names a specific place with a platform-resolved waypoint. It is corroborated by the driver's trace and, independently, by the rider's own admission against her interest. The excess is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied: this was the rider's own detour, no closure, amendment or pooled itinerary is on file to explain any part of it, so no residual excess survives and no distance or time refund runs back to the rider. Her fare of 12.53 stands.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the fact that decides this case, so it can be ruled on rather than sent to a human. [Rider], your in-app message at 11:37:10 on EV-CHAT-00520 — 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first?' — carries the platform-resolved waypoint (Sheng Siong Supermarket, Blk 501 Tampines Central 1), and your own statement ('I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true') confirms it. That is a rider instruction that is specific enough to act on and was sent inside the first minute of the trip, well within POL-RD-04's 3-minute window, and the trace (121 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gaps, 5.63 km driven) is consistent with a genuinely longer drive. The extra distance is therefore rider-caused and is excluded before the deviation and fare-recomputation clauses run.

[Driver], that exclusion cuts both ways. It means the fare you billed stands, but it also means the same clause's compensation limb applies to you: EV-FARE-00520 shows the rider was billed distance_charged_km 3.1 (the booked optimal), while EV-GPS-00520 records trace_distance_km 5.63 — an unbilled shortfall of 2.53 km, past the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, 2.53 x 0.75 = SGD 1.8975, rounded up to SGD 1.90, far under the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. That is the sum you contested and it is granted as DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Per POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd carries the same SGD 1.90; this is a platform-side payment for unbilled distance, not a second charge to the rider, whose SGD 12.53 charge stands.

[Rider]'s request for a distance/time refund is declined. Her advocate asked for the POL-RD-02 recomputation (charged_total SGD 12.53 less recomputed_fare SGD 8.605 = SGD 3.925, i.e. SGD 3.95), and the arithmetic is correct, but POL-RD-04 removes the rider-caused excess from the deviation before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, so that recomputation does not run and no part of the fare is returned.

Figures used: charged_total SGD 12.53; booked optimal distance 3.1 km; trace distance 5.63 km; unbilled distance 2.53 km; rate SGD 0.75/km; compensation SGD 1.90. No traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no external-cause exoneration was available — but neither party relied on a traffic cause, so it changes nothing. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no 500 m jump, no sampling interval over 30 s), and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. No repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 trips), so there is no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and with no ERP gantries or airport surcharge there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. All artifacts carrying the deciding facts — the chat log, the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown — are at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is 0.90.

ledger.claim: The governing distance measure is the GPS polyline, not the rounded trip-record copy. EV-GPS-00520 records trace_distance_km 5.63 against a booked optimal of 3.1 km on EV-TRIP-00520; the excess is 2.53 km, or 81.6% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment limbs pass (81.6% > 20% and 2.53 km > 0.8 km) and the excess also crosses the 50% material-deviation gate, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The trace that carries the finding is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 121 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0. There is no gap over 90 seconds (limb a), no 500 m jump between consecutive fixes (limb b) and no sustained interval above 30 seconds (limb c), so the impairment consequences in POL-RD-07 do not fire, the finding may rest on the gps_trace alone under POL-RD-08(b), and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Nothing moves the baseline off the booked optimal route: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route; trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play; and pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal. POL-RD-02 therefore runs against the booked 3.1 km / 6.0 minute optimal, not against some larger figure the driver might prefer.

On POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary: charged_total 12.53 on EV-FARE-00520 less recomputed_fare 8.605 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.1 + 0.28 x 6.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee — leaves 3.9250, which the platform's own derived figures publish as a payable refund of SGD 3.95 once rounded up to the nearest 0.05. It clears the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and is 31.3% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's remedy on this record is a partial refund of about SGD 3.95 and not nothing.

The rider's chat message on EV-CHAT-00520 does record a request to stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501, so POL-RD-04 can excuse part of the excess — but only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and the record nowhere quantifies that figure: the derived GPS block reports a single material deviation and no waypoint-attribution distance at all. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact for the exoneration he invokes, and an unquantified attribution cannot FULLY excuse a 2.53 km excess. To the extent it excuses part, POL-RD-02 still runs, and runs against the adjusted optimal route.

POL-RD-04 excludes excess DISTANCE and nothing else: unlike POL-RD-03, which spells out how an adjusted optimal's duration is derived (scaled by the ratio of adjusted to booked distance), POL-RD-04 carries no duration limb, so the booked 6.0-minute optimal duration governs the POL-RD-02 recomputation. The rider was billed 20.0 charged minutes at 0.28/min — a time_fare of 5.60 — against that 6.0-minute optimal. Whatever the detour attribution does to the distance line, the excess time charge the rider actually paid is not reached by POL-RD-04 and remains refundable under POL-RD-02.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip. EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING), so it can carry no fact and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run by anyone: no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the trace, or supports a leave-and-rejoin. No external traffic or closure exoneration is therefore available to cut down the measured excess.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and this case is triable on a monetary ruling rather than held. The trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00520, EV-GPS-00520 and EV-FARE-00520; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no timestamps run backwards (the trace runs 11:36:40 to 11:56:40); the POL-RD-02 refund of 3.9250 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total 12.53; and every charge line — base fare 3.80, distance 2.33, time 5.60, platform fee 0.80, zero ERP — has its counterpart in the trip record.

POL-RD-08's extra corroboration condition does not bite on this rider: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, below the 4-claim trigger, and the excess at 81.6% is itself above the 30% threshold the condition names. The deviation claim therefore needs no corroboration beyond the gps_trace.

The driver's SGD 1.90 is the POL-RD-04 compensation limb — 2.53 unbilled kilometres at 0.75, rounded up — and it is both discretionary ('may be granted') and conditional on the same rider-attribution the exoneration limb requires, measured against the trace rather than the trip record's rounded copy. It is not a refund of the fare and it must never be set against any POL-RD-02 refund the rider is owed: POL-GEN-03 requires a rider refund and a driver payment to be recorded independently, and forbids netting them.

The rider herself asked for the extra stop, in the in-app chat: at 11:37:10 she wrote 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something'. That is a rider-side instruction, so POL-RD-04(a) is satisfied on the face of the export.

The instruction is timely under POL-RD-04(b): the trip record shows the journey started at 11:36:40 and the rider's request was sent at 11:37:10 and delivered at 11:37:11 — inside the first minute of the trip and far within the three-minute window the clause allows after the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor.

The message is not the vague 'go the fast way' the clause excludes. It names a specific place and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint — 'Sheng Siong Supermarket, Blk 501 Tampines Central 1', lat 1.3549, lng 103.9458 — so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test is runnable on the record rather than undecidable as it would be on a null hint. The rider's own counter-statement confirms the point: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.'

The gps_trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 121 fixes over 20 minutes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 s (well under 90 s) and a sustained sampling interval of 10 s (well under 30 s). There is accordingly no POL-RD-10(3) escalation on this trace and the case is decidable on the present record.

The trace corroborates a genuinely longer drive on this trip: the driven polyline measures 5.63 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 3.1 km, a measured excess of 2.53 km or 81.6% over optimal. That is the signature of a stop at the rider's off-corridor Sheng Siong waypoint, and the rider admits she asked for it.

The driver was billed for less distance than the trace records, and the shortfall is large: fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 3.1 km, equal to the booked optimal, while gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 5.63 km — 2.53 unbilled kilometres, comfortably past the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. The rider paid for the route she booked, not the route she asked the driver to drive.

The compensation follows arithmetically under POL-RD-04: 2.53 unbilled kilometres at SGD 0.75 per kilometre is SGD 1.8975, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 1.90 — the exact sum the driver contests. The SGD 15.00 per-trip cap is nowhere near reached.

Even if the deviation were treated as standing rather than exonerated, it is MATERIAL (81.6% exceeds the 50% material threshold), so POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile check — and that check comes back clean. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, below both the three-flag test and the 0.05 ratio test. No pattern is established, so the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) and the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) are both unavailable; the profile fields used are the two POL-RD-06 names and no other, per POL-GEN-01.

To the extent the excess is attributable to the rider's own recorded instruction, POL-RD-04 requires it to be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, so no distance-or-time refund runs back to the rider and the charge already levied against her stands. The money that moves on this case therefore moves to the driver: under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd carrying the same SGD 1.90 figure as driver_compensation_sgd.
